history.summary: NOT A HINDU TEMPLE - keep-or-drop decision needed: this is a chief's tomb / memorial site, not a temple. Vanhnuailiana was an Eastern Lushai chief (father of Lalburha Sailo) whose settlement the British Cachar Column reached at the onset of the Lushai Expedition of 1871-72, after his death during the expedition. British expedition accounts describe his tomb as well preserved: many posts and heads, a broken Burmese idol inside, decorated with a large mithun skull whose horns impaled and carried a human head and arm, with headhunted remains of Sukte villagers outside; the expedition burned his settlement but left the tomb intact, converting the headhunted remains into a proper burial place (per Wikipedia's Vanhnuailiana and Lalburha articles, citing expedition histories). The tomb's original settlement lay south-east of Champhai. A 'Vanhnuailiana Memorial Park' is listed at Tualte, Khawzawl/Champhai area (796310), ~16 km from Champhai town; it is unclear whether the modern memorial park marks or relates to the 1871 tomb site (verify before treating them as the same referent). The CSV town 'Champhai' is therefore approximate; coordinates given are town-level for Champhai. The entry is retained here as a historic memorial site rather than a religious building.

name: Tomb of Vanhnuailiana

town_description: Champhai is a bustling commercial town at the Indo-Myanmar border, about 186-188 km east of Aizawl, considered the fruit bowl and rice bowl of Mizoram and a storehouse of ancient relics, legends and folklore. It was the headquarters of Lalbura Sailo, son of Vanhnuailiana, the Mizo chief against whom the British Expedition of 1871-72 was directed. Nearby attractions include Kungawrhi Puk cave, the Tiau river, Rih Dil lake across the border, and Thasiama Seno Neihna.
